rows.label: rem:morphisms_analytical_two_equal
rows.notes: IsAEMorphismOf.eq_of_eqOn: [IsRigidAction G X] [PreconnectedSpace M] [T2Space N], W open and W.Nonempty, f1 f2 a.e. morphisms for the SAME (arbitrary) atlases A, B; conclusion f1 = f2. PreconnectedSpace M with W nonempty is exactly DEC-42's 'M connected, open set nonempty'; N Hausdorff is part of the singular-manifold hypothesis; A, B need not even be a.e. atlases, so this is at least as strong as the paper under the ruling. The proof is genuine (clopen argument on the portly R = U1 ∩ U2, rigidity at closure points, density extension). Singular-manifold form IsAEMorphism.eq_of_eqOn present. Both counterexamples verified: id vs translation by 1 on R agree on ∅; on R ⊕ R (locally connected, Hausdorff, second countable, maximal atlas) id vs Sum.map id (+1) agree on range inl. The mark is licensed by DEC-42 ('Both rows close under these readings') and kb/0022 (after a ruling the hypothesis row reads 'carried').

rows.label: lem:aepullback
rows.notes: GX.aepullback proves (1) existence of an a.e. atlas making f an a.e. morphism, (2) any two a.e. atlases making f an a.e. morphism have the same maximal atlas (SameAEStructure), (3) ∃! maximal one (existsUnique_aePullback). (3) is DEC-42's 'uniqueness among maximal a.e. atlases'; (2) is the l.471 identification. SameAEStructure is not trivialising: on maximal atlases it is equality (IsMaximalAEAtlas.sameAEStructure_iff). Weakenings are genuine: B any a.e. atlas (the paper's is maximal), M locally connected and Hausdorff unused. The atlas the proof obtains 'by usual results' is constructed (A0 and its maximal atlas), not assumed. The non-uniqueness counterexample is verified: translationAtlas vs {refl} on R are distinct a.e. atlases both making id an a.e. morphism (the restriction of refl to (0,1) lies in one and not the other).

rows.label: prop:GX_sing_morph_local
rows.notes: The paper defines neither 'locally an a.e. morphism' nor the a.e. structure induced on a subset; the reading (IsAEMorphismOn: some U ⊆ W portly in W on which f is regular for the ambient atlases) is disclosed in SCOPE (d) and asked as a question (kb/0011). All four implications are proved; isAEMorphism_tfae is the singular-manifold form. DEC-42 does not settle the reading.

rows.notes: 0 ∉ Reg(z ↦ z^p) for p ≠ 1 is proved for arbitrary atlases (p = 0 included), and with lem:regf1 not_isAEMorphismOf_pow gives 'the Lemma would force p = 1'. The sentence about Riemann surfaces and 'maps locally modelled on z^p' (only the literal z^p on C is treated) are not formalized, disclosed in SCOPE (g). No ruling; partial is correct.

rows.label: cor:locally_connected_hausdorff_topological
rows.notes: The corollary states no hypothesis making g^*A and f^*g^*A defined; aePullback_comp_of_exists proves it whenever the left side is defined (and yields existence of (g∘f)^*A), aePullback_comp under the a.e.-local-homeomorphism hypotheses of lem:aepullback. Both genuine. No ruling accepts the presupposition, so partial with the question is the honest status.

issues.problem: 'f is a.e. a local homeomorphism' is undefined in the paper and is read from the proof's first line (portly O, portly P ⊆ supp B, f(O) ⊆ P). The plainer reading 'f is a local homeomorphism on some portly O' is not bridged in Lean. Under the paper's own hypothesis M locally connected the readings coincide (take O ∩ f⁻¹(supp B), portly by IsPortly.inter_preimage_of_isLocalHomeomorphOn, and P = supp B), so nothing is lost, but the closed row rests on a reading the REPORT does not list as a question.
